newsitem.title: GEORGIA: Ramco considers oil projects in ex-Soviet Georgia.
newsitem.headline: Ramco considers oil projects in ex-Soviet Georgia.

text.p: Ramco Energy Plc chairman Stephen Remp met Georgian officials on Friday to discuss participation by the Scottish-based oil independent in energy projects in the former Soviet republic.
"Georgia does not exist on the map as an oil country yet," Remp told reporters after meeting President Eduard Shevardnadze. "But Ramco would like to be here as soon as possible."
He said Ramco had agreed to send specialists to Georgia soon to define possible exploration and development projects.
Georgia, on the Black Sea, is better known to Western energy investors as a key oil transport link between Kazakh and Azeri projects and Western markets.
Ramco has a 2.1 percent stake in an $8 billion international consortium in the Azeri sector of the Caspian Sea that will send some of its early production to Western markets via Georgia.
Ramco has said that it is closely eyeing Georgia, where local officials have said offshore reserves may total 200-300 million barrels.
